extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy/classics (readers of Plato's Republic)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements Plato articulates for the education, character, epistemic attainment, and political role of philosopher-rulers (guardians) in the ideal city-state, including the stages and methods of learning and the rare combination of qualities required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper timing and ordering of philosophical study
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy study must be ordered so as not to ruin the State: ‘In childhood and youth their study, and what philosophy they learn, should be suited to their tender years’; as intellect matures, increase the 'gymnastics of the soul'; when civic duties cease, allow free philosophical life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not begin full dialectic in early childhood; shape bodily training first, then progressively more intellectual training. Education must be staged: bodily formation in youth, increasing intellectual rigor as maturity arrives, and leisurely contemplation in later life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of a true philosopher (moral dispositions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true philosopher is a lover of truth, gentle and free from envy, not given to making 'persons instead of things the theme of their conversation', and avoids detraction and malice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate philosophers by their love of truth and nobility of temper; avoid pretenders who busy themselves with personalities and quarrels. Philosophers should imitate fixed and immutable order and be reverential toward the divine pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of philosopher-rule or philosophically-inclined rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: Either philosophers must be compelled to take charge of the State (though they may be 'useless but not corrupt') or rulers (kings/sons of kings/princes) must be divinely inspired with a true love of philosophy for a State to attain perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ideal polity requires that those who rule understand and love philosophy; either rulers must be philosophers or rulers must be trained/inspired to pursue philosophical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing guardians by trials of pleasure, pain, hardship and patriotism
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians are to be lovers of their country, tried by the test of pleasures and pains: 'he was to be rejected who failed, but he who always came forth pure, like gold tried in the refiner’s fire, was to be made a ruler.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for office requires real-world probations (hardships, dangers); only those who remain steadfast and patriotic under trial are eligible for rulership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of broad intellectual training and endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspiring rulers must be 'exercised also in many kinds of knowledge, to see whether the soul will be able to endure the highest of all, or will faint under them'; they must take a 'longer circuit' to reach highest knowledge, not be content with partial accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess candidates by breadth of study and their capacity to pursue difficult, extended intellectual work (not merely superficial or popular expositions). The guardian must both 'toil at learning as well as at gymnastics.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of the Good as the highest requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest knowledge is the idea of the good: 'the idea of good is the highest knowledge, and that all other things become useful and advantageous only by their use of this.' Without knowledge of the good no other knowledge will profit a guardian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers must possess an understanding of the Good (the cause of truth, science, and being). Mere technical or moral knowledge without grasp of the Good is insufficient for guiding the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite intellectual and temperamental qualities are necessary (rarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The combination required (quick intelligence, memory, sagacity, cleverness, high spirit, magnanimity, and steadfastness) rarely grows together; some are quick and impetuous, others steadfast but torpid toward intellectual toil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating suitability, require both vivacity of intellect and stable, disciplined temperament; acknowledge the scarcity of such ideal individuals ('they are mostly found in shreds and patches').

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of knowledge and faculties (the divided line)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four levels: (1) perception of shadows (opinion), (2) faith/conviction (belief about visible objects), (3) understanding (mathematical/geo-type sciences using hypotheses), and (4) reason/dialectic (knowledge of first principles). Corresponding faculties: perception, conviction, understanding, reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate intellectual attainment by where it falls on the divided line: the highest office requires ascent to dialectic (reason) rather than remaining at opinion or merely understanding sciences that depend on hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of dialectic (method) over hypothesis-bound arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplines like geometry use hypotheses and aim at ideals, but dialectic 'passes out of hypotheses' to first principles: 'the soul passes out of hypotheses, and goes up to a principle which is above hypotheses...in and through the ideas themselves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers should be trained in dialectical method—able to move beyond assumptions to first principles—rather than only competent in arts that rely on unexamined hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as a painful, gradual ascent (allegory of the cave)
rubrics_metrics.description: The allegory shows prisoners seeing only shadows; release and ascent to the light cause pain, dazzlement, and a staged acclimatization (shadows → reflections → objects → stars → sun). Returning to the cave, the enlightened will be mocked or killed by those who prefer shadows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational programs for guardians must be gradual and recognize resistance: initial discomfort is expected; allow time to adjust to higher truths. Prepare for social hostility to those who return from higher knowledge to lead ordinary citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative design: erase the existing picture and copy the heavenly pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: When designing constitutions, 'they will begin by taking the State and the manners of men, from which, as from a tablet, they will rub out the picture, and leave a clean surface' and then 'trace an outline of the constitution' by looking to absolute justice and beauty as a model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional reform should start by clearing corrupt or accidental practices before inscribing laws; continually compare human institutions to the ideal (heavenly) pattern and mix elements to approximate it.
